headline: PSX bounced, but the tape is still being steered by oil and the Strait-of-Hormuz shock.
summary: PSX recovered 1,646.81 points (+0.98%) to 170,511.85 on hopes of easing Gulf-Iran tensions, but that followed Thursday's 3,078.56-point drop and Brent still near $107. August remittances of $3.656bn help the external account, while 11.1% CPI and the September 14 SBP meeting keep the rate backdrop tight. The desk's read is still defensive: large banks keep the cleanest carry case, E&P has oil support but not immunity, and cyclicals need the oil/geopolitical pressure to cool before their setups deserve trust.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Large banks still benefit from government-paper carry while SBP is expected to hold at 11.5%; UBL and MCB also screen with covered dividends in the retained fundamental file.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas E&P
sectors.why: Oil above $100 supports OGDC, PPL and MARI fundamentals, and Lundali-1 adds production, but the last week showed E&P can still sell off with the broader tape.

sectors.name: OMCs & refiners
sectors.why: The oil shock raises import and working-capital pressure; any benefit needs clearer pass-through than the desk has in state today.

sectors.name: Autos, cement & leveraged cyclicals
sectors.why: High oil, 11.1% CPI and no near-term rate-cut case leave this group exposed to cost and demand pressure.
